title: Morning Edition
intro: Nvidia’s leadership is under fresh scrutiny while AI systems keep moving into physical and financial operations. Today’s brief covers a new open robotics model, wallet integrations, a disputes around an FAA tool, and debate over CEO dependence.

items.title: Runway's open-source Praxis-1 turns video AI into a robot controller
items.summary: Runway releases its robotics model Praxis-1 with open weights and source code under the Apache 2.0 license. The model uses knowledge from video training for robot control and leads the World Action Model category on Nvidia's RoboLab-120 benchmark. It can't yet plan complex action sequences on its own, though. The article Runway's open-source Praxis-1 turns video AI into a robot controller appeared first on The Decode
items.why: Open weights and code let researchers test video-trained models for real-world robot control and measure limits in planning.
items.headline: Runway open-sources Praxis-1 robot model
items.aiSummary: Runway released Praxis-1 with open weights and source code under the Apache 2.0 license. The model uses knowledge from video training to control robots and leads the World Action Model category on Nvidia’s RoboLab-120 benchmark, though it cannot yet plan complex action sequences on its own.

items.title: Analysis: Companies love a ‘rockstar’ CEO. Until they depend on one
items.summary: Jensen Huang’s exit tests Nvidia’s succession planning and governance, and offers lessons for companies that elevate their CEOs to rockstar status.
items.why: The story highlights governance risks when a company becomes dependent on a single executive.
items.headline: Analysis: companies and the ‘rockstar’ CEO problem
items.aiSummary: CNBC examines how Jensen Huang’s exit tests Nvidia’s succession planning and governance. The piece draws lessons for firms that elevate CEOs to rockstar status.

items.title: Connect Google Wallet to Gemini for personal finance insights
items.summary: All Gemini app users in the U.S. can connect Google Wallet to get responses informed by their spending habits.
items.why: Linking Wallet and Gemini brings personal spending data into AI-driven answers for U.S. users.
items.headline: Connect Google Wallet to Gemini for spending-informed replies
items.aiSummary: All Gemini app users in the U.S. can connect Google Wallet. Connected users receive responses informed by their spending habits.

items.summary: After launching its Dots AI agents platform earlier this year, OpenAI is launching a wallet for the agents. ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out starting today for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US aged 18 and older using a US billing address and "eligible US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa cards." After adding a card […]
items.why: The wallet enables Dots agents to make purchases on behalf of eligible U.S. subscribers.
items.headline: ChatGPT Wallet rolls out for some US Pro subscribers
items.aiSummary: OpenAI is launching ChatGPT Wallet for its Dots agents platform, rolling out starting today for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the U.S. aged 18 and older with a U.S. billing address and eligible U.S.-issued AmEx, Chase, Mastercard or Visa cards.

items.title: AI company behind FAA's SMART tool denies link to ground stop, Duffy confirms
items.summary: Air Space Intelligence (ASI), the company behind a recently deployed Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) AI tool, denied any link to the nationwide ground stop issued Friday afternoon. “The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC,” the company...
items.why: The denial separates a recent FAA operational pause from the deployed AI tool and the vendor behind it.
items.headline: AI firm denies link between FAA ground stop and SMART tool
items.aiSummary: Air Space Intelligence said the nationwide ground stop was not based on or a result of the FAA’s SMART system, any product of ASI, or its integration with FAA and ATC. The company issued the denial after the ground stop was issued Friday afternoon.

items.title: The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
items.summary: I was certain, until the story of Jensen Huang's second affair hit, that Huang was bulletproof. After all, why wouldn't he be? He's placed himself indispensably at the center of the AI industry and famously had no succession plan at Nvidia. In fact, he's the only CEO Nvidia has ever had. L'état c'est moi. Then […]
items.why: The coverage underscores questions about leadership concentration and succession at a major AI chipmaker.
items.headline: The Jensen Huang scandal continues to roil Nvidia coverage
items.aiSummary: The Verge reports that a second affair involving Jensen Huang changed perceptions of him and notes he had no succession plan and is the only CEO Nvidia has ever had. The article frames Huang as having placed himself indispensably at the center of the AI industry.
